draft.emotion: warm and approving, nodding with a slight smile
notes: When placed before a masculine singular noun, 'buono' shortens to 'buon' wherever the indefinite article would be 'un' (e.g., 'un buon amico', 'un buon caffè', but 'un buono studente').
Do not confuse with 'bello' (beautiful/nice to look at, also used in 'bel tempo' for good weather) or 'bravo' (skilled, well-behaved).

faults.quote: Before a masculine singular noun starting with a vowel, s+consonant, z
faults.why: False grammar rule: 'buono' drops '-o' when 'un' is used, NOT before s+consonant or z.

faults.quote: Oggi c'è un tempo buono per andare al parco.
faults.why: Good weather in Italian is 'bel tempo', not 'tempo buono'.
